text:
amy_support: FYI customer Acme Analytics reporting spike of 502/504s to hosted inference for last ~12m. They saw TLS handshake timeouts and NXDOMAINs when we tried to contact their resolver. Raising for SRE :eyes:

ben_oncall: on it. Can you paste the trace + any edge logs? Also pinging @li_runtime in case it's an inference runtime fallback.

amy_support: attaching snippets:
```
edgegw-127: TLS handshake timeout to 198.51.100.7:443 after 15s
edgegw-127: resolver=198.51.100.7 returned NXDOMAIN for model-host.example.internal.
hosted-api: upstream 10.4.12.8 conn reset during cert refresh
```
Customer says failures started right after our scheduled cert rotation window (≈ 2026-03-17T15:00Z).

li_runtime: hmm. If resolver returned NXDOMAIN while cert rotation was fetching OCSP/CRL or pulling chain, the runtime could have tried fallback hostnames and tripped gateway 502. Do we have deploy logs for cert rotation?

deploy-bot: cert-rotation-job/2026-03-17-15:02 status=running nodes=prod-edge-*
deploy-bot: cert-rotation-job/2026-03-17-15:08 status=completed code=0

amy_support: dig from one of our edge boxes (at 15:04Z):
```
$ dig +short @198.51.100.7 model-host.example.internal A

;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NXDOMAIN, id: 2345
```
and a curl to upstream returned: `curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`

ben_oncall: looks like a resolver flap coincident with cert rotation. Two tracks: 1) fix customer impact now (workaround: force runtime to use alternate resolver or fallback to cached IP) 2) root cause (why did 198.51.100.7 return NXDOMAIN mid-rotation?). Can we repro from multiple regions?

amy_support: repro from us-east and eu-west edges. Customer reports increased client-side retries/timeouts and billing anomalies because of repeated token usage. Maya, can you coordinate customer-facing note?

maya_cs: on it — telling them we saw transient DNS flap during our cert refresh window, apologizing, offering credit if billing impacted. Will open support ticket with timeline.

li_runtime: quick mitigation: toggled resolver fallback to 1.1.1.1 on the affected edge pool and warmed route to the pinned model host IP. Monitoring for 10m.

ops-bot: routed traffic via fallback resolver 1.1.1.1 for pool prod-edge-3 at 2026-03-17T15:12Z

ben_oncall: after switching fallback resolver, 502s dropped to baseline within 3m. Suggest we add a short-term guard: during cert rotations, prefer cached A records for 30s and avoid fresh DNS queries for model hosts. li_runtime can we add config toggle?

li_runtime: yes — I'll push a 2-line config change to prefer cache during intensive control-plane ops. Will ship canary to prod-edge-3 now.

kb-bot: similar incident: 2025-11-09 DNS-propagation-during-cert-rotation caused gateway 502s — mitigation was resolver fallback + cache preference. See internal runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dns-cert-rotation

amy_support: customer confirmed degraded window ~15:00–15:13Z, now sending follow-up. Closing escalation once Li's config is in. Thanks team :thumbsup:

li_runtime: canary applied to prod-edge-3 at 2026-03-17T15:20Z, will roll to rest of pool in 10m if stable.

ben_oncall: root cause hypothesis: CA/OCSP requests during rotation increased control-plane lookups; one resolver returned NXDOMAIN (likely stale zone or rate-limited), causing our nodes to attempt fresh A lookups and hit client-side timeouts. Follow-ups: - confirm resolver operator logs for NXDOMAIN at 15:04 - add monitoring alert for NXDOMAIN spikes during rotation windows - update rotation job to stagger OCSP fetches

amy_support: noted. filing ticket and linking runbook. closing thread after postmortem notes.

maya_cs: sent customer note and credit offer. Customer accepted, impact limited.
